quickCards.title: Heat Wave Cool-Room Loop
quickCards.summary: Cycle shade, airflow, hydration, and room checks before the house gets dangerous.
quickCards.bodyMarkdown:
## First 10 Minutes
- Close blinds on sun-facing windows.
- Stage water, medications, and chargers in one cool room.

## Keep Doing
- Rotate people and pets through the cool room.
- Limit oven, dryer, and heavy appliance use until evening.

## Leave Early If
- Indoor heat keeps climbing.
- Anyone becomes confused, stops sweating, or cannot cool down.

## Do Not
- Trap everyone in the hottest room.
- Wait until the house feels dangerous before planning transport.

mediaAttachments.caption: A single cool room works best when shade, airflow, water, and key supplies are staged before the hottest part of the day.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing a shaded room with water, airflow, and household staging supplies.

questions.prompt: What should happen first when the indoor temperature starts climbing quickly?

options.text: Close sun-facing blinds and stage one cool room.
Open the oven to warm the kitchen less often.
Wait until the whole house feels dangerous.

questions.explanation: The drill starts with a single cool room: block direct sun, move essentials there, and reduce indoor heat sources early.

questions.prompt: Which sign means it is time to leave early instead of stretching the cool-room plan?

options.text: The room is quiet and shaded.
Someone becomes confused or stops cooling down.
The house is darker than usual.

questions.explanation: Confusion or failure to cool down are escalation cues. The card stays conservative and favors transport before the home becomes unsafe.

quickCards.title: Wildfire Smoke Clean-Room Setup
quickCards.summary: Build one lower-smoke room quickly and keep it clean enough to rest in.
quickCards.bodyMarkdown:
## Seal
- Shut windows and exterior doors.
- Block obvious drafts with materials you can remove fast.

## Filter
- Run the best filter setup you already know how to use.
- Keep doors closed once the room is staged.

## Protect
- Leave smoky jackets, shoes, and cleanup tools outside the room.
- Keep medications, water, and chargers inside.

## Move If Needed
- Indoor air keeps worsening.
- Anyone struggles to breathe or cannot recover after getting inside.

mediaAttachments.caption: Seal the room, run the best filter setup you already trust, and keep smoke-covered gear outside the clean room.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing a sealed window, an air filter, and staged medications and water inside a clean room.

questions.prompt: What belongs inside the clean room once it is staged?

options.text: Only the filter and nothing else.

questions.explanation: The card keeps the clean room practical: medications, water, and chargers stay inside so people can recover there.

questions.prompt: When should the household move instead of trying to force the room to work longer?

options.text: When indoor air keeps worsening or someone cannot recover after getting inside.
As soon as the sky looks hazy outside.
Only after the filter makes noise.

questions.explanation: The drill is conservative: worsening indoor air or ongoing breathing distress are leave-early cues.

weeklyDrillMetadata.prompt: Call out the seal-filter-protect order before smoke gets heavy indoors.

quickCards.title: Flood Water Entry Stop-Check
quickCards.summary: Use a stop-check-move sequence when water is rising or entering the home.
quickCards.bodyMarkdown:
## Stop
- Pause before troubleshooting.
- Check footing, exits, and who still needs to move.

## Check
- Note where water is entering and what outlets or appliances are nearby.
- Lift documents, lights, and medications above the expected water line.

## Move
- Shift go-bags, chargers, and dry layers toward the safest exit.
- Leave before stairs, doors, or roads are cut off.

## Do Not
- Keep wading once you lose dry footing.
- Reset gear while water and electricity risks are still unclear.

mediaAttachments.caption: As water rises, pause, check hazards and exits, then move essentials toward the safest exit before footing is lost.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing a rising indoor water line with supplies lifted above it and an exit direction.

questions.prompt: What happens before you start troubleshooting where the water is coming from?

options.text: Pause and check footing, exits, and who still needs to move.
Walk deeper into the water to inspect the outlet.
Reset appliances so they stop floating.

questions.explanation: The drill begins with stop-check-move. Stability and exits come before troubleshooting.

questions.prompt: Which action belongs in the move step?

options.text: Keep wading until the room is dry.
Shift go-bags, chargers, and dry layers toward the safest exit.
Stay put until the road is cut off.

questions.explanation: The move step is about getting essentials and people toward a safe exit before access narrows.

weeklyDrillMetadata.title: Flood Exit Drill
weeklyDrillMetadata.prompt: Run the stop-check-move sequence before the water line reaches outlets or stairs.
